study_material.title: Clocks - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Clock problems are angle arithmetic: the minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute, the hour hand 0.5 degrees per minute. One formula gives the angle at any time; relative speed logic gives coincidences and right angles.
learning_objectives: Compute the angle between the hands at any time
Find when hands coincide, oppose or form right angles
Use the 55-minute gain of the minute hand

concepts.heading: 1. Hand Speeds
concepts.body: Minute hand: 360 degrees in 60 min = 6 deg/min. Hour hand: 360 in 12 hours = 0.5 deg/min. Relative speed = 5.5 deg/min - the minute hand gains 5.5 degrees on the hour hand every minute.

concepts.heading: 2. The Angle Formula
concepts.body: Angle at H hours M minutes = |30H - 5.5M| degrees (take 360 minus the result if it exceeds 180). Example 3:30 - |90 - 165| = 75 degrees. Example 4:20 - |120 - 110| = 10 degrees.

concepts.heading: 3. Coincidences and Oppositions
concepts.body: Hands coincide when the gap closes to 0: once every 65 5/11 minutes, i.e. 11 times in 12 hours, 22 times a day. They are opposite (180 apart) 11 times in 12 hours too; at right angles 22 times in 12 hours, 44 times a day.

concepts.heading: 4. Gaining and Losing Clocks
concepts.body: A clock gaining k minutes per hour shows 60+k minutes for every true 60. Convert between true and shown time with the ratio. A clock that is 10 minutes fast SHOWS a later time; correct by subtracting.

formulas: Minute hand speed 6 deg/min, hour hand 0.5 deg/min
shortcut_methods: Hands coincide between H and H+1 at 60H/11 minutes past H
Mirror-image time = 11:60 minus the given time (approximately, for reflection questions)
common_mistakes: Forgetting the hour hand moves during the minutes
Reporting reflex angles (>180) instead of the standard angle
Assuming right angles happen 48 times a day (it is 44)
study_material.summary: One formula (|30H - 5.5M|) plus the 5.5 deg/min relative speed answers nearly every clock question.

solved_examples.question: What is the angle between the hands at 3:30?
The angle between the hands at 6:00 is:
solved_examples.step_by_step: Hands point at 12 and 6: straight line, 180 degrees.

solved_examples.question: Find the angle between the hands at 4:20.
solved_examples.shortcut: Hour hand has crept 10 degrees past the 4.

solved_examples.question: How many times do the hands of a clock form a right angle in 24 hours?
solved_examples.step_by_step: 22 times per 12 hours (some hours share events), so 44 per day.

practice_questions.question: The angle between the hands at 9:00 is:
The minute hand moves how many degrees in one minute?
In 20 minutes, the hour hand moves:
The angle between the hands at 7:30 is:
The angle between the hands at 2:20 is:
In 12 hours, the hands of a clock coincide:
practice_questions.explanation: They coincide every 65 5/11 minutes: 11 times per 12 hours.

practice_questions.question: At what time between 1 and 2 o'clock do the hands coincide?
A clock gains 5 minutes every hour. If set right at 7 am, what does it show at 7 pm the same day?
practice_questions.explanation: 12 true hours x 5 min gain = 60 min extra: shows 8:00 pm.

questions.explanation: It passes all 12 numbers in 12 hours.

The angle between the hands at 8:15 is:
At what time between 4 and 5 o'clock are the hands together?
A watch loses 3 minutes every hour. Set right at 6 am, what true time has passed when it shows 6 pm the same day (shown 12 hours)?
questions.explanation: It shows 57 min for each true 60: true = 720 x 60/57 = 757.9 min = about 12 h 38 min.
